aiSummary: The OnePlus Buds 4 is positioned in the premium mid‑tier Indian TWS market at ₹6499, relying on a feature‑rich stack (ANC up to 55 dB with dynamic real‑time adjustments, LHDC 5.0 hi‑res codec, 11mm woofer + 6mm tweeter, IP55, Bluetooth 5.4 with dual‑device connectivity, 47 ms game latency, Google Fast Pair, and adaptive modes) to justify the price and appeal to music enthusiasts and OnePlus ecosystem users. The listing signals solid demand and availability (In stock) with meaningful volume (about 1K+ units sold monthly) and strong CPU‑category placement (Top 50 Electronics, #47 In‑Ear Headphones), plus color variants Zen Green and Storm Gray that broaden appeal and support cross‑selling via variant SKUs. Customer sentiment via reviews is broadly positive on sound quality, ANC, and dual connectivity, yet there are material caveats: battery life is inconsistent across users, reliability issues (left/right earbud failures, LHDC stability) surface in reviews, and there is a perceived gap due to lack of wireless charging and variable long‑term durability. This creates a risk of mixed word‑of‑mouth if reliability remains a pain point, despite a high average rating (~4.3 from thousands of reviews) and strong perceived value in this price tier. The brand leverages OnePlus ecosystem advantages (Oxygen OS compatibility, LHDC support on capable devices, Google Fast Pair) and a rich media/asset set (gallery, high‑res images, A+ content, video count) to bolster trust and conversions, but reliance on ecosystem‑dependent features may limit appeal for non‑OnePlus devices unless cross‑brand performance is clearly demonstrated. Opportunities include adding wireless charging or a lower‑price tier to sharpen price competitiveness, expanding ear‑tip sizes to improve fit (addressing mixed fit feedback), and investing in long‑term reliability improvements (quality control for buds and case, LHDC stability) to reduce negative reviews. Marketing should emphasize multi‑device convenience, adaptive ANC/value, and the “Hi‑Res LHDC 5.0” claim while setting realistic expectations on battery life variability. In summary, the product demonstrates strong market demand, compelling feature breadth, and effective brand leverage, but sustained growth hinges on tightening reliability, expanding comfort options, and potentially broadening charging/feature parity to defend against commoditization in a competitive segment.

features: [Industry leading ANC up to 55 dB & 5500Hz range]: Powered by the latest OnePlus algorithms, Buds 4 can dynamically adjust ANC in real time—up to 800 times per second—based on ambient noise to ensure optimal noise cancellation. [All-New Adaptive Mode] Dynamically switches between ANC and Transparency Modes for safer and smoother listening.

[Flagship level near-lossless sound]: Featuring twin tailored DACs (Digital-to-Analog Converter), an 11mm woofer and a 6mm tweeter, precisely engineered to deliver powerful bass and clear treble, creating rich lows and pristine highs across a wide soundstage. Industry leading Hi-res Codec of LHDC 5.0 and upto 1 Mbps 24-bit 192kHz LHDC 5.0 meets studio-grade Hi-Res for silky-smooth sound with reduced latency.

[Steady Connect | AI translation] Steady connect ensures reliable connectivity both indoors & outdoors. It ensures ultra strong bluetooth with massively extended range up to 250 meters(For select OnePlus phones with Oxygen OS15.0.0 & above). With AI translation, break the language barrier. Experience seamless real-time conversation in many languages. [IP55 Rating]: With IP55 dust and water resistance, you’re protected against sweat and rain—no worries, just music.

[Customizable settings for hassle free control]: Slide up/down for volume control, Long touch/hold to switch among ANC, adaptive & transparency mode, single tap for play/pause,double or triple taps for switching songs. [47ms low latency in game mode]: Low latency ensures every gunshot, footstep, and game alert syncs perfectly with your actions, providing users with a smoother and more enjoyable gaming experience.

[Fast charing & longer battery life]: Large battery delivers up to 45 hours of non-stop music with ANC Off; A quick 10-minute charge delivers up to 11 hours of music playback. [Dual-Device Connection | BT5.4 | Google Fast Pair ]: Simultaneously connect to two devices (Android/iOS/Windows smartphones, tablets or computers) for quick and seamless device switching, Google fast pair simplifies the pairing process, Voice assistant shortcut (Google Gemini, Google Assistant or Apple Siri) to help you with various tasks.

The fit receives mixed reviews, with some finding it comfortable while others say it doesn't sit snugly.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Update 2:Finally achieved very good sound profile when I enabled dolby Atmos in my mobile. That pretty much solved all my issues with sound profile not being rich. So if anyone is having such an issue then enable dolby Atmos in your cellphone if your phone supports it. Then play with Equalizer  a bit to get incredibly rich and balanced output. Otherwise I won't recommend this. Better get a bud for 1500 bucks. The sound of that won't be any inferior to this without dolby Atmos support.Update1:Sound Profile: Initially I thought the default sound profile was balanced but then I heard some of my favourite songs and the default profile is definitely bass heavy, not at all my kind of sound. I like balanced. I installed heymelody app for this bud and tweked the sound essentially lowered the bass substantially and increased the mid and high frequencies. Bass is still good but the overall sound signature became balanced. Now it's much much better.Noise cancellation: The noise cancellation is quite good and sometimes I do go in that mode especially in high noisy area and it's brilliant in that situation. Otherwise I disable it.Fit: Fit is very good for my ears so no issues there.Battery: The battery backup i have not measured but is substantial that I haven't noticed anything peculiar. Should be in the ballpark figure of what's claimed.Orginal post:It is a decent ear buds. I have never used noise cancelling earbuds and this is my first one. I was always doubtful if I enjoy it, and that seems to be the case. Noise cancellation is a bit uncomfortable (not the buds, they are a good fit). I felt uneasy, so I disabled noise cancellation and now it's fine.As far as the sound signature is concerned, it is good. Decent balanced sound output. Nothing bad, nothing exceptional.Connectivity wise there is no problem. I have not checked the range but it shouldn't be a problem for normal use case.  Call quality over phone is good but I have not checked in outdoor condition.The earbuds are decent fit, I haven't had any issue with fit.Overall, a decent buy for the price.

I’ve been using the OnePlus Buds 4 since September 24, 2025, and even after long-term daily use, they continue to perform exceptionally well.The highlight feature is Golden Sound once you complete the ear scan and setup, the audio becomes noticeably personalized and immersive. The sound feels fuller and more engaging, to the point where you can actually feel the music. What makes this feature even better is that it works across any device, not just OnePlus phones, which is a big advantage over many ecosystem-locked competitors.The Active Noise Cancellation is genuinely effective for everyday use, handling background noise well without feeling artificial. Battery life has also been reliable: the earbuds provide around 5–6 hours of continuous playback, and the charging case offers approximately 4–6 full recharges, making it easy to get through a full day or more without worry.The build quality is durable to a reasonable extent, though rough use especially with the black variant can lead to visible scratches. My unit is the black color, which looks very dignified, remains lightweight, and is easy to carry without feeling bulky. Despite being plastic, the buds feel far more premium than most in this segment; in hand, they could easily be mistaken for metal or another high-grade material.Overall, the OnePlus Buds 4 focus on delivering strong fundamentals sound quality, ANC, and dependable battery life and they do so consistently, making them a very satisfying long-term purchase.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I had the goated oppo enco air 3 pro, they got stolen and then I had purchased these at 4.7k after doing some research. It has been almost a month so here's my review:TLDR: Everything is great apart from tuning-- it sucks! I had to spend so much time tuning them to overcome their muddy bassy sound output and get the sound signature I require that I'll deduct a point specifically for that. They have responsive DACs so once I tuned them I really enjoyed the sound imaging and clarity these presented.Pros:1. ANC (all the modes are useful)2. Call quality (no complaints)3. Dual device connectivity (a minor setback here is you'll have to manually pause the current device's playback to switch to other)4. Battery life works well (I use 4-5hrs/day and I charge 1-2 times a week)5. Sounds imaging and clarity6. Responsive towards custom EQ7. Build quality feels premium8. Touch controls are goodCons:1. Tuning: the stock tuning is a muddy bassy sound, it misses the mids altogether. You can cover up mids to some degree using hey melody app's custom EQ. But it will still sound muddy.I have spent more than 20 hours playing around with different EQs. Here's what works for me:1. Turn on golden sound (tunes the buds wrt your ears)2. Turn on 3d sound (opens up the sound stage)3. Keep the inbuilt EQ of hey melody completely flat.4. Install wavelet, and tune the output by increasing the mids(refer to attached image)This tuning works well for most songs and you can play around if you want.So overall, after tuning these buds they become almost perfect and I am happy with them.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Excellent for Music EnthusiastsExcellent for Music Enthusiasts
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I bought the OnePlus Buds 4 in December and used them for about 20 days, switching from Samsung Galaxy Buds 2. Compared to the Buds 2, these feel much lighter with a better IP rating perfect for gym workouts. Sound quality shines for music lovers: well-balanced audio clean singer vocals, strong bass, clear treble and excellent separation that fully satisfies. Noise cancellation, transparency mode and call quality work reliably too.Drawbacks: no wireless charging (Buds 2 has it) average battery life and slightly overpriced. Overall worth it if music, movies and calls are your priorities.
